newsitem.title: USA: Hurricane watch issued in Caribbean.
newsitem.headline: Hurricane watch issued in Caribbean.

text.p: A hurricane watch was issued for the British Virgin Islands, U.S. Virgin Islands and Puerto Rico on Saturday as Tropical Storm Hortense moved toward the Caribbean, gaining strength, the National Hurricane Center.
Tropical storm warnings also were in effect from Martinique in the eastern Caribbean northwestward through Puerto Rico.
A hurricane watch indicates that hurricane conditions are expected within 36 hours. Hurricane and tropical storm warnings are posted by forecasters 24 hours ahead of possible landfall.
At 5 p.m. EDT (2100 GMT), Hortense was located about 35 miles (56 km) east of Guadeloupe and Dominica, at latitude 15.9 north and longitude 60.9 west.

The storm carried maximum sustained winds of about 60 mph (95 kmh) and was moving west-northwest at 10 mph (16 kmh), a track that forecasters said was expected to continue for the next 24 hours. Further strengthening also was likely by Sunday evening, the National Hurricane Center said.
Hortense would become a hurricane if sustained winds reached 74 mph (119 kmh).
"On this track the storm will be passing through the Leeward and northern Windward Islands today and Sunday," said Ed Rappaport of the National Hurricane Center.
Hortense gathered strength in the wake of Hurricane Fran, which hit the U.S. coast on Thursday, wreaking havoc through the Carolinas and leaving at least 21 people dead.
Hortense was upgraded to tropical storm status at mid-morning on Saturday.

The string of tiny Leeward Islands -- including Martinique, Dominica, Guadeloupe, Antigua, Montserrat, the U.S. Virgin Islands and the British Virgin Islands -- immediately issued tropical storm warnings and urged residents to prepare.
Forecasters said it was too early to predict whether Hortense would threaten the U.S. mainland.
"It's way too early to know if the continental United States is going to be affected. There's so much time that any number of factors could turn it away," Rappaport said.
In three days Hortense was expected to be near Haiti and the Dominican Republic, which share the island of Hispaniola. The island is about 700 miles (1,126 km) south of Florida.
Tropical storm force winds extended outward up to 85 miles (140 km) east of the center.
Hortense was also dumping rain of up to 10 inches (25 cm) along its path. Forecasters warned that even more rain could fall as Hortense moved over mountains, increasing the risk of flash floods.
